big: A headline says mutual funds saw a ₹1.83 lakh crore outflow in a month. It sounds like panic. But the same month, retail equity investors added money. The outflow came from companies parking and pulling cash around tax dates.

lines: A huge outflow! Are people fleeing funds?
Ask which category, which investor, and what month. Liquid funds are used by companies as a cash account. Big redemptions near advance tax dates are routine.

rows: Yes: tax dates in Jun, Sep, Dec, Mar
note: Advance tax falls on 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March.

title: Flow headlines
stops: Liquid funds follow corporate cash cycles
Quarter-end outflows always mean retail panic
A headline can mix very different investors
caps: Firms use them like a current account.
Retail equity may be rising at the same time.
Always ask which category and investor.

q: A headline reports a huge outflow in a quarter-end month. What is the first question?
opts: Which fund house is to blame here?
Who wrote the headline, and when?
Is the market about to crash soon?
why: Splitting by category and investor reveals the real cause.
Blame is not the point of the analysis. The details here point elsewhere.
The writer does not explain the flow. That does not match this case.
A flow headline does not predict a crash. It does not fit the facts given.

q: Why do liquid funds see heavy redemptions near 15 June, September, December and March?
opts: SEBI closes the funds each quarter
why: Retail interest is not the reason.
SEBI does not close funds each quarter.
Advance tax instalments fall on those dates.
Funds do not stop paying returns at those dates.

q: Who mainly uses liquid and money-market funds in large amounts?
why: Large flows are not mainly from first-timers. It does not fit the facts given.
Firms use them as an alternative to current accounts.
Retired individuals are not the main users. The details here point elsewhere.
Trustees are one small group at most. The details here point elsewhere.

q: Debt outflow is large, but retail equity inflow is strong that month. What is the sound reading?
opts: Retail investors are all confused today
The market must be about to fall
The two figures must be wrong
why: Retail inflow shows steady behaviour, not confusion.
Flow data cannot call a fall. It does not answer what was asked.
Both can be right, as they cover different groups.
Corporate cash and retail equity follow different drivers.

pts: Liquid fund flows follow corporate cash cycles.
Advance tax dates: 15 Jun, Sep, Dec, Mar.
Break a headline into category, investor and season.
